name: settings.py
summary: Django settings module centralizing runtime configuration, environment variable ingestion, and project-wide constants for the conversationalBI backend.
purpose: Separates configuration from code to support multiple deployment environments while keeping secrets and environment-specific parameters out of version control, leveraging django-environ for type-safe parsing.
responsibilities: Ingest and validate environment variables via django-environ and os.environ
Define Django core settings including INSTALLED_APPS, MIDDLEWARE, DATABASES, and TEMPLATES
Establish base project paths using pathlib.Path
Configure security controls (SECRET_KEY, DEBUG, ALLOWED_HOSTS, CSRF/TRUSTED origins)
Set up static and media file handling, including storage backends
Define logging, timezone, and internationalization defaults
Expose third-party service credentials (databases, caches, APIs)
inputs: Optional .env file entries parsed by django-environ
Filesystem layout via pathlib.Path and os
outputs: Fully populated Django settings namespace imported by the WSGI/ASGI application
Typed configuration values consumed by Django and third-party packages
Resolved absolute paths for static, media, and template directories
architecture_notes: Implements the 12-Factor App config principle by externalizing configuration into the environment. The module serves as the composition root for the Django framework, translating the external deployment context into a strongly typed internal representation. Co-locating Path, environ, and os imports indicates a hybrid approach to path resolution and env-var management; placing settings under backend/config/ hints at a dedicated configuration package that could be extended into a split-settings hierarchy (base/local/production).
improvements: Decompose the monolithic file into a settings package with base.py, local.py, and production.py to eliminate conditional environment logic
Implement mandatory environment variable validation that fails fast with actionable messages when required variables are absent
Remove any hardcoded secrets or default fallback values for SECRET_KEY and database credentials
Adopt pathlib.Path exclusively and remove os.path usage for consistency
Add a __all__ or typed Settings class to improve IDE autocompletion and static analysis
Introduce a SETTINGS_SCHEMA or JSON Schema export for DevOps validation and documentation
